title: An adult child gets a discharge date and becomes the operations manager for an aging parent

actor.context: Parent can no longer safely manage alone

job: Build a safe care plan across public programs, private care and family capacity.
trigger: Hospital discharge, fall, cognitive decline or caregiver burnout creates a hard deadline.
surfaceComplaint: I do not know what services exist, what we qualify for, or who is covering tomorrow.
mechanism: Capacity shortage matters, but the acute burden is coordination across eligibility, assessments, public waitlists, private providers, family shifts and changing needs with no single accountable operator.

actors.incentive: safe care without collapse of own life

economics.painCostNote: Recurring operational pain: paid care plus caregiver work loss and emergency escalation.

buyer.roiLogic: Small relative to sustained care spend and caregiver time.

distribution.acquisition: Trigger-based professional referral is more credible than broad consumer marketing.

competitors.gap: optimizes own service, not family system
software can augment scarce expert capacity

intervention.notBuildYet: No clinical judgments or promises of caregiver supply.

experiment.sample: 10 families within 14 days of care crisis
experiment.artifactRequest: discharge/assessment docs + current services + weekly availability
experiment.outreach: discharge planner + geriatric clinic + caregiver ERG
experiment.success: 5/10 pay C$500+ and save 5+ hours or avoid one coverage failure
experiment.kill: cannot enter without licensed care partner, or every plan is too bespoke

claims.text: Toronto HMNS uses eligibility screening and a waitlist.
The family coordination burden extends beyond finding a caregiver.
